look_here_first: Check a mature middle leaf: triangular/deltate to ovate with a continuous margin bearing teeth but NOT deep lobes or dissections; opposite leaves and blue-violet rayless heads support Conoclinium. Compare C. dissectum's palmately cut foliage.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: opposite triangular/deltate leaves with 3 strong basal veins; rhizomatous colony-forming perennial; flat-topped to domed array of many small blue-violet heads; heads are discoid: disk florets only, no rays; cypsela topped by capillary pappus

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Triangular to deltate, serrate/dentate, strongly 3-veined from base.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Small blue-violet discoid heads with no ray florets.

key_traits.label: Reproductive confirmation
key_traits.text: FNA: corollas usually 2–2.5 mm; cypselae 1–1.5 mm glabrous.

lookalikes.differences: Versus C. dissectum: intact triangular/deltate toothed blades rather than deeply lobed; shorter glabrous 1–1.5 mm cypselae vs longer hispidulous 1.8–2.5 mm. Versus Chromolaena odorata: Conoclinium has short hemispheric involucres, not long cylindrical 8–10 mm ones.
